original_card.question: Does a new paid-profile or mixture-ceiling claim have independent source-bound coverage of its actual changed ledger?
methods: Independently reconstruct one changed paid ledger or pooled dual with exact source and model binding.
Check a genuinely uncovered moment implication with a different enclosure method and semantic controls.
original_card.acceptance_gate: Demonstrate independence, source binding, positive cases and semantic failure controls. Name the existing checks and the missing coverage. More digits or another equivalent evaluation of an unchanged root is not by itself new verification coverage.

first_step.inspect: Choose one uncovered implication in #4088 literal mixed fill, #4091 pooled dual/model binding or #4067 changed frame/host bill. #4091 pins an earlier #4088 head: validate word, capacity and stock equivalence before applying that ceiling to the later fill.
first_step.scope: Source-binding orientation only; no scientific replay, theorem acceptance or supplier admission. Budget any heavy replay separately.

original_card.first_experiment: Independently reconstruct one changed ledger or pooled certificate with a positive case and a semantic failure control. Compare exact sources and name what existing checks miss. Keep this separate from supplier-boundary-audit (ordinary/outer dispatch) and uniform-transfer-audit (all-size proof). Stop after the chosen implication; more digits of an unchanged root are not additional mechanism coverage.
original_card.bottleneck_link: Independent pricing prevents unsupported frontier claims and can reveal genuine accounting slack.
allowed_variations: Reconstruct either a source ledger or a numeric enclosure with a different method.
scope_change_triggers: Importing the primary function and calling its output independent verification.
Calling an aggregate histogram or source archive an independently accepted physical supplier.

actual_scope: Independent check of one hand-argued claim of open PR #4628 (head ee4fd87f): the engine-game bound of at least 2.9447 calls per array from block 4 on (2.99172 at block 5, 2.97290 at block 6), obtained by projecting the block-4 hook profile through symplectic reductions. Re-derives the projection counts, recomputes the recursion and the all-m tail with own exact code, reconstructs a soundness argument, and isolates which block-4 inputs the numbers rest on.
scope_change_reason: The card's examples (#4088, #4091, #4067) concern the bit-side paid ledgers; this package applies the card's method (independent reconstruction of a paid profile with source binding, positive cases and semantic failure controls) to the paid-call profile of the complex small-block lower bounds in #4628, which nobody had checked independently.
bottleneck_link: Side result for the complex small-block line: it decides how much weight the open-case table of #4628 (2 in 7 and 3 in 9 at blocks 5 and 6) can carry. No new kappa and no claim about integer multiplication.
stop_rule: Stop after the projection-recursion claim is reconstructed, recomputed and its inputs isolated; do not recompute block-4 hook ranks.
evidence: verify.py: brute-force projection counts over all 15/135/2295 Lagrangians at m = 2, 3, 4 (sample at m = 5); exact T_5 = 834241/278850, T_6 = 1188222/399685, min over m = 5..60 = 2.944709234; dominating-chain inequalities for k <= 300 (proved for all k in README) and c* = 2.944709234 > 2.9447; sensitivity to the block-4 inputs; 10 failure controls rejected.

open_questions.question: Are the block-4 hook values a_3 >= 68,320 (enters T_5) and a_2 >= 48,576 (enters T_6) correct as lower bounds on the raise of a rank-3 and rank-2 Clifford?
open_questions.why_it_matters: They are the only inputs of 2.99172 and 2.97290 that rest on a single author program (mod-p ranks, no stored certificate, not re-checked by #4628's verify.py); with the triangle bounds alone the numbers drop to 2.832 and 2.772.
open_questions.first_step: Store an explicit nonzero minor (or a rank certificate over one character block) for C_e0 C_e1 C_e2 on the k = 8, f = 9 hook and check it with a separate checker, as was done for the demand 86,592.
open_questions.blocked_by: Size: the hook has dimension 102,960; a character-block split as in hookG is needed.

open_questions.question: Can the induced-representation argument of README section 2 be written as a full proof (or in Lean) on the engine's own definitions?
open_questions.why_it_matters: The author's written proof (PROOF.md Theorem 3 of the pf-induction track) is in a private archive; this package gives an independent sketch, not a checked proof.
open_questions.first_step: Formalise the step 'program right at every width => identity in C[G]' (Burnside-Brauer for the finite Clifford group) and the decomposition raise_U(g) = sum_q raise(reduced g).

open_questions.question: Does any certificate exclude 3 in 9 at block 5 or 6 (needs more than 3 calls per array)?
open_questions.why_it_matters: It is the smallest engine-game shape at blocks 5 and 6 that no stated bound excludes; this projection route stays below 3 at both blocks (2.99172, 2.97290) and its limit is 2.94471.
open_questions.first_step: Run the same recursion from a block-5 base profile with top ratio above 3 (for example a block-5 hook at larger width), if one can be computed.
open_questions.blocked_by: #4628's own ceiling notes say projection gains at most a factor 1.1 and hook-type certificates stay below 4.
